The course is divided into the following modules, which are studied with the help of web based course material, supported by one lecture occasion per module:
1. Work and technology on human terms
2. Physical load + Physical factors + Chemical health risks in working life
3. Methods + Design processes
4. Occupational injuries + Work environment and economics + Work environment legislation + Standardisation
5. Psychosocial work environment + The organisation of production and work
6. Human-technology systems + Safety and risk

The course consists of four individual written analyses, including peer feedback, of a case that accompanies the course throughout modules 1–4. The case analyses include mapping occupational health and safety risks in a work environment and developing proposals for measures based on knowledge acquired through the web-based learning material as well as current research findings. Before each module, a lecture session will be offered where we will jointly summarize the key messages of the module, discuss aspects that may be difficult to understand, and explore how the module’s content can be applied to the case. In addition to the lecture sessions, the course coordinator will be available for questions during two scheduled hours per week. Modules 5 and 6 are covered in seminar format (mandatory attendance). The course also includes an occasion with mandatory study visits to the various work environment-related laboratories operated by Ergonomics and Aerosol Technology.

Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5) - (Fail, Three, Four, Five)
Assessment:
For a passing grade the student must hand in approved written case analyse, actively participate in the mandatory seminars, and pass the oral exam.

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.

Modules
Code: 0112. Name: Working Environment, Occupational Health and Safety. 

Credits: 7.5. Grading scale: TH - (U, 3, 4, 5).
        
          Assessment: For a passing grade the student must hand in approved summaries of all modules in the web-based course material, and receive a passing grade on connecting the case to the modules, approved peer-review, as well as active participation in the final student group discussion.

Aim
The aim of the course is for students to:

acquire fundamental knowledge that will enable them to consider work science aspects in their future places of work.
understand the interaction of work environment factors of a technological, economic, medical, psychological, and sustainable nature.
acquire basic skills in identifying and solving work science problems, according to the sustainability goals in Agenda 2030, in existing settings as well as in the design of new work organizations, jobs and workplaces.

Knowledge and understanding
      For a passing grade the student must

Competences and skills
      For a passing grade the student must
With respect to health risks, systematically survey, analyse and suggest improvements in work organizations, jobs and workplaces With respect to conditions that promote health and sustainability, systematically survey, analyse and suggest improvements in work organizations, jobs and workplaces with respect to criteria for comfort, satisfaction and personal development, systematically survey, analyse and suggest improvements in work organizations, jobs and workplaces With respect to different production conditions and demands, systematically survey, analyse and suggest improvements in work organizations, jobs and workplaces

      For a passing grade the student must
Present the work carried out in a reflective and analytical way in written reports and in the oral student group discussion.

In addition to the lecture sessions, the course coordinator will be available for questions during two scheduled hours per week. Modules 5 and 6 are covered in seminar format (mandatory attendance).
